name: Polar Circle Air-Cruise
flight: Round trip: fly south, fly north

seo.title: Polar Circle Air-Cruise by Antarctica21: 10 Days
seo.description: Fly over the Drake Passage from Punta Arenas, then sail the Antarctic Peninsula south toward the Polar Circle on an 88-guest Magellan ship. Ten days, February only.

tagline: Fly the Drake, then sail south toward 66 degrees 33 minutes.
answer: The Polar Circle Air-Cruise is Antarctica21's ten-day, nine-night voyage from Punta Arenas, Chile. Guests fly about two hours to King George Island, then spend six days aboard Magellan Explorer or Magellan Discoverer, 88 guests at most, sailing the western Antarctic Peninsula and aiming far south toward the Polar Circle. It runs in February.
overview: Antarctica21's longest air-cruise on the Peninsula. After the flight in, the ship spends Days 3 to 8 between the South Shetland Islands and the western Antarctic Peninsula, with daily Zodiac landings, small group hikes and exploratory Zodiac outings.
The route is set by ice and weather. Antarctica21 says it may include the Gerlache and Penola straits and Crystal Sound, with the goal of sailing far south toward the Polar Circle.

itinerary.summary: Arrive in Punta Arenas and transfer to the hotel. Check in at Explorers House before 2 PM for the mandatory briefing, then the welcome dinner.

itinerary.summary: Landings and Zodiac cruises among the South Shetland Islands, chosen by the expedition team on the day.

itinerary.title: Exploring Antarctica: western Peninsula
itinerary.summary: Northbound landings and Zodiac outings along the western Peninsula.

itinerary.title: Exploring Antarctica: South Shetland Islands

itinerary.place: King George Island to Punta Arenas
itinerary.summary: Fly from King George Island back to Punta Arenas and transfer to the hotel for the night. Meals in Punta Arenas that evening are at your own expense.

faqs: Do you cross the Antarctic Circle?

Antarctica21 describes the goal as sailing far south toward the Polar Circle, via waters that may include the Gerlache and Penola straits and Crystal Sound. Ice and weather decide how far the ship gets.
Do I have to sail the Drake Passage?
No. You fly over it both ways, about two hours from Punta Arenas to King George Island.
Magellan Explorer and Magellan Discoverer, each with a maximum of 88 guests on air-cruises.
February. Antarctica21 announced two departures in each of the 2026-27 and 2027-28 seasons. Exact dates are not in the page text.
What happens if weather delays the flight?

Antarctica21 flies only when King George Island weather allows. Outbound, it keeps trying from Day 1 until 2 PM on Day 4, with Punta Arenas tours, meals and the Day 1 hotel covered while guests wait. If guests still cannot fly by then, the trip is cancelled and Antarctica21 refunds 100% of the cruise fare. On the way back, the ship keeps cruising until the flight is cleared, or guests fly up to a day early.
How much luggage can I take on the flight?

25 kg (55 lb) per person in total, hand luggage included, with no single item over 20 kg. Extra allowance cannot be bought. On the Classic and Polar Circle air-cruises, excess luggage is held in Punta Arenas until you return.
